cues.en: or at least surviving, the Battle of the  Atlantic and making sure these convoys kept
cues.zh: 至少是生存的关键，是大西洋战役的关键，也是确保这些护航船队持续

cues.en: getting through. And just to show you the value,  there's a graph of the tonnage of Allied shipping
cues.zh: 通过的关键。为了展示其价值，这里有一张图表，显示了战争中盟军航运逐月被击沉的吨位，

cues.en: being sunk month-by-month through the war, and  also the number of U-boats that we were sinking
cues.zh: 以及我们在战争中击沉的U型潜艇数量。

cues.en: through the war. And if I tell you that there was  a period in the middle of the war, when the naval
cues.zh: 如果我告诉你，在战争中期有一段时间，德国海军

cues.en: German Navy decided to upgrade to their Enigma  machine, and they added a fourth rotor to it.
cues.zh: 决定升级他们的Enigma密码机，并给它增加了第四个转子。

cues.en: And that shut out Bletchley from naval Enigma for  about ten months until they'd caught up with this
cues.zh: 这使得布莱切利园在大约十个月内无法破解海军Enigma，直到他们赶上这个进展，

cues.en: and rebuilt their processes. If you look at that  chart, you can tell exactly when that four months
cues.zh: 并重建了他们的流程。看看那张图表，你能准确看出那四个月的时段

cues.en: was, and it's right there. That is the value of  being able to read your enemy's communications,
cues.zh: 就在那里，这正是能够读取敌人通信内容的价值所在，

cues.en: and being able to decrypt them. Because convoys  losses here went up from 150,000 tonnes a month
cues.zh: 并且能够解密它们。因为这里的护航损失从每月15万吨上升了

cues.en: to 700,000 a month almost overnight, and if losses  had continued at that rate the war would probably,
cues.zh: 几乎一夜之间达到每月70万，如果损失继续以那个速度发展，战争很可能，

cues.en: certainly in the Atlantic, have been lost.  So that's the context of the cryptanalysis,
cues.zh: 当然，在大西洋中，有些已经失传了。这就是密码分析的背景，

cues.en: the cryptography game of Bletchley. So now let's  take a little bit of a digression and we've got
cues.zh: 布莱切利的密码学游戏。现在我们稍作离题，我们有了

cues.en: to introduce some terminology about cryptography,  and we do this quite gently because it gets quite
cues.zh: 先介绍一些密码学的术语，我们会讲得很轻松，因为这部分内容其实挺……

cues.en: complex later on. So we have a plain text, we're  going to call that P, and you put that through
cues.zh: 比较复杂。所以我们有一段纯文本，我们把它叫做 P，然后你把它放进

cues.en: some process that munches it all up and ciphers it  and encodes it and you end up with the cipher text
cues.zh: 某个进程把它全部处理掉，加密它，编码它，最后得到密文

cues.en: and we call that Z. So P becomes Z. The simplest  way of doing that and way we all know we probably
cues.zh: 我们称之为Z，于是P变成了Z。最简单的方法，也是我们都熟悉的做法，可能

cues.en: all do this children at school, is called an  alphabetic substitution cipher, where you've
cues.zh: 学校里孩子们都在做的这个，叫做字母替换密码，在这里你

cues.en: just got two alphabets: an input alphabet and  output alphabet. And you encode letter by letter,
cues.zh: 刚得到两个字母表：一个输入字母表和一个输出字母表。然后你逐字母编码，

cues.en: just by translating from one to the other. Very  very simple. That was used over 2,000 years ago
cues.zh: 仅仅通过从一个翻译到另一个。非常非常简单。那在2000多年前就被使用了

cues.en: by Julius Caesar, and we often refer to it as a  Caesar cipher. Now that thing and techniques like
cues.zh: 由Julius Caesar提出，我们常称之为Caesar密码。现在这个东西以及类似的技术

cues.en: it is very easy to break using simple frequency  analysis - different letters in the English
cues.zh: 用简单的频率分析就很容易破解——英语里的不同字母

cues.en: language occur with different frequencies, you can  count up the frequencies and you can guess which
cues.zh: 不同语言出现的频率不同，你可以统计这些频率，从而猜测哪些

cues.en: cipher letter corresponds to which plain letter  and you can work backwards and you can break
cues.zh: 密文字母对应哪个明文字母，然后你可以倒推破解

cues.en: things fairly easily. Now to make it a bit more  complicated, you use a more complicated scheme
cues.zh: 东西还挺容易的。现在让它稍微复杂一点，你用更复杂的方案

cues.en: called a polyalphabetic substitution cipher.  Now here you've got a multitude of alphabets,
cues.zh: 这叫做多表替换密码。现在你有了多个字母表，

cues.en: that example there has three, and you just use  them in rotation. So the first character gets its
cues.zh: 那个例子有三个，你轮流使用它们。所以第一个字符得到它的

cues.en: cipher using the first alphabet, the second with  the second one, and the third with the third one,
cues.zh: 第一个字母用第一套字母表，第二个用第二套，第三个用第三套，

cues.en: then you go back to the first one, and so on.  That's much, much harder to break because unless
cues.zh: 然后回到第一个，依此类推。这样破解起来就难得多，因为除非

cues.en: you know how many alphabets there, are you don't  know how to break down this this cipher text into
cues.zh: 你知道有多少个字母表，否则你就不知道如何把这个密文拆分成

cues.en: subsets, and then carry out frequency analysis  on the subsets and work backwards to what all
cues.zh: 子集，然后对子集进行频率分析，再反推回去，弄清楚

cues.en: the individual alphabets are. Now, it's possible,  but it's much, much harder and that is what Enigma
cues.zh: 各个字母表分别是什么。这现在是可能的，但难度要大得多，而这就是 Enigma

cues.en: does. Enigma generates essentially a non-repeating  sequence of 16,900 alphabets one after the other.
cues.zh: 所做的。Enigma 本质上会依次生成一个不重复的、包含 16,900 个字母表的序列。

cues.en: Now the average message sent with Enigma was only  a few hundred characters, so the alphabets never
cues.zh: 而用 Enigma 发送的消息平均只有几百个字符，所以在一条 Enigma 消息中，这些字母表

cues.en: repeat in an Enigma message. That's what makes  Enigma much, much, much harder to break. Frequency
cues.zh: 从不会重复。这就是 Enigma 破解起来要难得多的原因。频率

cues.en: analysis is essentially impossible. And an Enigma  message as it arrived at Bletchley looked like
cues.zh: 仅凭分析基本不可能破解。而一份送达布莱切利园的 Enigma 消息看起来是这样的，

cues.en: that, that's a photograph of a real one, and you  can see it's been transcribed from Morse by one
cues.zh: 那，那是一张真实机器的照片，你可以看到它是由某个监听站从摩尔斯电码转写而来的。

cues.en: of the listening stations. Up here tells you when  it was transcribed and likely where it came from,
cues.zh: 上面这部分告诉你它是什么时候被转写的，以及大概来自哪里，

cues.en: and what frequency it was received on and  what-have-you. And that was fed into the
cues.zh: 还有接收频率之类的信息。然后这些就被送进布莱切利园的

cues.en: codebreaking industry at Bletchley and broken.  But then in early 1941 they started hearing a
cues.zh: 密码破译部门并被破译了。但到了1941年初，他们开始听到一种

cues.en: completely different kind of transmission. And it  looked like this. It's very high-speed automated
cues.zh: 完全不同的传输方式。它看起来是这样的。这是非常高速的自动化

cues.en: transmission. So it's not standard Morse with a  key, it's been generated by a machine. So they
cues.zh: 传输。所以它不是用按键发出的标准摩尔斯电码，而是由机器生成的。于是他们

cues.en: built little ticker tape machines that would  transcribe this into into ones and zeros and
cues.zh: 造了些小纸条机器，把内容转写成0和1，

cues.en: printed out on a little ticker tape and then it  would be hand transcribed into letters. Because
cues.zh: 打印在小纸带上，然后手工转写成字母。因为

cues.en: it turns out, it's a standard international  telegraph alphabet. And if you look as they did,
cues.zh: 这其实是标准的国际电报字母表。如果你像他们那样，

cues.en: at the network on which this traffic appeared, you  can use traffic analysis and direction-finding to
cues.zh: 去查看这些通信出现的网络，就能用流量分析和测向来

cues.en: work out where that network is and who's connected  to what. And the first thing you notice about it
cues.zh: 推断出那个网络在哪、谁连着谁。你首先会注意到的是

cues.en: is it's not used very much. This is quite a,  quite a sparse network. It's also very long
cues.zh: 它用得不多。这是个相当、相当稀疏的网络。而且还跨

cues.en: distance and it's centres on Berlin. So the kind  of guess is that this is very high-grade traffic
cues.zh: 很长距离，中心在柏林。所以大致可以猜这是非常高级别的通信

cues.en: it goes direct to Nazi High Command in Berlin,  and if we could break into it, this would be very
cues.zh: 它直接发往柏林的纳粹最高统帅部，如果我们能破译它，这将非常

cues.en: very useful indeed. So, they started looking at  it and the first person to look at it was a guy
cues.zh: 非常有用。于是他们开始研究它，第一个研究它的人是个叫

cues.en: called John Tiltman and he established that it was  something called a Vernam cipher. He was unable to
cues.zh: John Tiltman的人，他确认这是一种叫做Vernam密码的东西。他无法

cues.en: analyse it far enough to do anything with it,  but he established that it works like this:
cues.zh: 分析到足以对它做任何事的程度，但他确认了它的工作原理是这样的：

cues.en: So you take your message and you convert your  plain text using a standard teleprinter alphabet
cues.zh: 你取出你的消息，用标准电传打字机字母表把你的

cues.en: into 5-bit binary representation. And that's the  standard International Telegraph alphabet number
cues.zh: 明文转换成5位二进制表示。那就是标准的国际电报

cues.en: two. It's perfectly standard, nothing unusual  about that. And then you combine it with a key
cues.zh: 二号字母表。完全标准，没有什么不寻常的。然后你把它与一个密钥

cues.en: string using what they called "carry-less binary  addition" but we know as "exclusive or". So you
cues.zh: 他们用所谓的“无进位二进制加法”来加密字符串，而我们称之为“异或”。所以

cues.en: exclusive or that, bit-wise, with some kind of  pseudorandom key stream. And the key stream we
cues.zh: 把那个与某种伪随机密钥流按位异或。这个密钥流我们

cues.en: call K, and the result is your cipher text: Z.  Okay so it's a binary addition or binary operation
cues.zh: 称为 K，结果就是你的密文：Z。好，所以这是一种二进制加法或二进制运算

cues.en: which now we call exclusive or. And this process  works backwards as well, just like Enigma does,
cues.zh: 我们现在叫它异或。这个过程也可以反向进行，就像 Enigma 一样，

cues.en: so you take this and you add it back to the  key stream and you get the plain text down so
cues.zh: 所以你把它加回密钥流，就能得到明文，

cues.en: it's it's a reversible process. That's one of the  properties of exclusive or, if you've studied that
cues.zh: 这是一个可逆的过程。这是异或的特性之一，如果你学过的话

cues.en: as I'm sure you have. That if you add something  back to itself, the original result comes out.
cues.zh: 我相信你学过。如果你把某个东西加回它本身，原始结果就会出来。

cues.en: So very, very simple. So, the receiving operator  would simply take this, punch it on a tape, feed
cues.zh: 非常简单。接收操作员只需把它打在纸带上，送入

cues.en: it into the machine set up exactly the same way  as the originating machine - and out would come
cues.zh: 把它装到一台配置与原机器完全相同的机器上，出来的就会是

cues.en: the plain text. Very, very simple. So Tiltman got  that far and no further. Then they had an enormous
cues.zh: 纯文本。非常非常简单。Tiltman 就做到这一步，再没有更进一步。然后他们有一个巨大的

cues.en: stroke of luck. 31st of August 1941, an operator  in Vienna sent a message that did not get through.
cues.zh: 运气真好。1941年8月31日，维也纳的一名操作员发了一条没发出去的消息。

cues.en: So the recipient asked him "could you send that  again please 'cause I missed it." And, breaking
cues.zh: 于是收件人问他：“你能再发一遍吗？我刚才没收到。”然后，打破

cues.en: all the rules, he reset his machine to the same  original settings and typed out the message
cues.zh: 他把机器重置回最初的设置，然后打出了那条消息

cues.en: again. But he didn't quite send it exactly the  same way, 'cause he was a bit bored and probably
cues.zh: 又一次。但他发送的方式并不完全相同，因为他有点无聊，可能还

cues.en: a bit tired, maybe it was the end of the day, he  used some abbreviations in the second message so
cues.zh: 有点累了，可能是到了下班时间，他在第二条消息里用了些缩写，所以

cues.en: it wasn't quite exactly the same, it was a little  bit shorter but it saved in time typing it out. So
cues.zh: 内容并不完全一样，稍微短了点，但省了打字的时间。所以

cues.en: there are the two messages, and you can see that  they were both over 4,000 characters long the
cues.zh: 这两条消息在这儿，你能看到它们都超过了4000个字符，前

cues.en: first 12 characters are the same and it starts the  same, and then you can see it starts to diverge.
cues.zh: 12个字符是一样的，开头相同，然后你能看到它开始出现分歧。

cues.en: So, Tiltman guessed, that standard operating  procedures in German encryption meant the first
cues.zh: 所以Tiltman猜测，德国加密中的标准操作流程意味着前

cues.en: 12 characters basically told the receiving  guy "this is the way I set my machine up",
cues.zh: 12个字符基本上是在告诉接收方“这是我设置机器的方式”，

cues.en: so we can ignore those because we don't know what  they mean. But the rest of it was the message,
cues.zh: 所以我们可以忽略这些，因为我们不知道它们是什么意思。但其余部分是消息本身，

cues.en: and he noticed the second message started the  same but then it started to get different. Now,
cues.zh: 他发现第二条消息开头也一样，但后面就开始不同了。那么，

cues.en: being a Vernam cipher, which we know how that  works too - he knew that they would be encrypted
cues.zh: 作为一个Vernam密码，我们也知道它的原理——他知道这些消息会用

cues.en: using the same key stream, and if you add the two  messages together in binary, what happens is the
cues.zh: 相同的密钥流加密，如果把两条消息按二进制相加，结果就是

cues.en: key disappears. Okay? Because they're both added  together with the same key. Add them together and
cues.zh: 密钥消失了。明白吗？因为两者都是用同一个密钥相加的。把它们加在一起，

cues.en: the key actually disappears so what he ended up  with was the two messages added together. So:
cues.zh: 密钥实际上就消失了，所以他最终得到的是两条消息相加的结果。所以：

cues.en: cipher text 1 cipher text 2. Add them together  and so by comparing these two messages and very
cues.zh: 密文1加上密文2。把它们加在一起，然后通过比较这两条消息，并非常

cues.en: carefully guessing at what the first character  was, subtracting it from the other one, and seeing
cues.zh: 仔细地猜测第一个字符是什么，从另一条中减去它，再看看

cues.en: if that made sense, and then letter by letter,  trying to go forward through and forwards and
cues.zh: 如果这说得通，然后一个字母一个字母地，试着向前推进，再向前，

cues.en: backwards constantly subtracting each one from the  other to see if he could make sense of it. He did,
cues.zh: 再向后，不断把两者相减，看他能否理解其中的含义。他做到了，

cues.en: eventually, after ten days, managed to break  out the message - both of them in fact. 4,000
cues.zh: 最终，在十天后，成功破译出了消息——实际上两条都破了。长达4000

cues.en: characters long. Now that in intelligence terms  is useless, because the message is about six weeks
cues.zh: 个字符。从情报角度看，这已经没用了，因为这条消息到现在已经

cues.en: old by now. So the content of it is useless, but  he then realized that if we take these two plain
cues.zh: 大约六周了。所以它的内容已经没用了，但他随后意识到，如果我们把这两段明文

cues.en: texts and we add them back together, what you  get is the keystream. So he managed to produce
cues.zh: 加回去，得到的就是密钥流。于是他成功生成了

cues.en: 4,000 characters of the keystream, which doesn't  sound massively useful but actually turns out to
cues.zh: 4000个字符的密钥流，这听起来不太有用，但实际上却证明

cues.en: be worth its weight in gold. They looked at it for  about three months, they analysed it to death and
cues.zh: 价值连城。他们研究了大约三个月，反复分析到极致，却

cues.en: couldn't come up with with any deductions from it  at all. Until they gave it to a guy called Bill
cues.zh: 完全得不出任何推论。直到他们把它交给一个叫 Bill

cues.en: Tutte - another Cambridge mathematician. Cambridge  2, Oxford nil. So he took it away, locked himself
cues.zh: Tutte 的人——又一位剑桥数学家。剑桥得 2 分，牛津挂零。他把资料带走，把自己关在

cues.en: in his room, and by writing the keystream out  in grids again, and again, and again, in grids
cues.zh: 房间里，通过把密钥流一遍又一遍地写成网格，用不同大小、

cues.en: of different sizes and different repeats - huge  quantities doubtless of pencils and coffee and
cues.zh: 不同重复模式的网格——无疑耗费了大量铅笔、咖啡和

cues.en: paper, he managed to work out the entire structure  of the machine from four thousand characters of
cues.zh: 纸张，他竟从四千个字符的密钥流中推算出了这台机器的

cues.en: the keystream. Now just remember that I showed  you a picture of one of those teleprinters right
cues.zh: 完整结构。现在请记住，我刚才给你们看过其中一台电传打印机的照片，就在

cues.en: at the beginning of the presentation. No-one  in Britain had seen one of those machines,
cues.zh: 在演讲开始时，英国没有人见过那种机器，

cues.en: and no-one did until after the war ended. But  without seeing one, Tutte managed to work out the
cues.zh: 直到战争结束后才有人见到。但图灵在没有见过机器的情况下，成功推算出了

cues.en: entire internal structure of the machine what he  deduced is that it didn't just have three wheels
cues.zh: 机器的整个内部结构，他推断出它不像Enigma那样只有三个轮子，

cues.en: like enigma does it had twelve quite a complex  machine he also managed to work out the number of
cues.zh: 而是有十二个，相当复杂的机器。他还成功算出了

cues.en: bit positions the number of steps on each wheel  and he identified that they were in three sets
cues.zh: 每个轮子上的位数和步数，并确认它们分为三组轮子，

cues.en: of wheels the first set he called these the Chi  wheels and they advanced as a group one position
cues.zh: 第一组他称为Chi轮，它们作为一个整体每经过一个字符就前进一个位置，

cues.en: for every character that went through the machine  generating a random pseudo-random bit stream of
cues.zh: 生成一个随机的伪随机比特流，

cues.en: five bits. The second set, he called those the  Psi wheels, nobody quite knows why. But they
cues.zh: 五个比特。第二组，他称之为 Psi 轮，没人太清楚为什么。但它们

cues.en: moved approximately 50% of the time, so roughly  every other character but in a random sequence.
cues.zh: 大约有 50% 的概率转动，所以大致每隔一个字符，但顺序是随机的。

cues.en: And they generated another pseudo-random sequence  of five bits. And this third set of two wheels in
cues.zh: 它们生成另一串五个比特的伪随机序列。而中间这第三组两个轮子，

cues.en: the middle, he called those the motor wheels or  the Mu wheels, and they controlled this stuttering
cues.zh: 他称之为马达轮或 Mu 轮，它们控制着末端 Psi 轮的那种

cues.en: movement of the Psi wheels on the end. Tutte,  after the war, moved to Canada and he was awarded
cues.zh: 断续转动。Tutte 战后移居加拿大，被授予

cues.en: the Officer of the Order of Canada I guess that's  a Canadian equivalent of an OBE or something,
cues.zh: 加拿大官佐勋章，我猜大概相当于英国的 OBE 之类，

cues.en: I don't know. And in the citation for that,  what he achieved here, was described as one
cues.zh: 我也不确定。在授勋的赞词里，他在这里取得的成就被描述为一项

cues.en: of the greatest intellectual feats of World War  II. It's quite an astonishing piece of work. So,
